title: Russia Holds Scaled-Down Victory Day Parade; North Korean Troops March for First Time
detail: Russia held its annual Victory Day parade on Red Square on May 9, 2026 — scaled back without tanks, armored vehicles, or ground weapons for the first time in nearly two decades, with only a flyover of combat jets. For the first time, North Korean troops marched in the parade — a tribute to Pyongyang's contribution to Russia's Kursk campaign, where approximately 10,000 North Korean soldiers fought against Ukrainian forces. Foreign leaders attending included Belarusian President Lukashenko with his son Nikolai, and the presidents of Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan. The parade proceeded under tight security amid the US-brokered three-day ceasefire in the war.

media.caption: Russia's scaled-down Victory Day parade on Red Square, May 9 2026, with North Korean troops marching for the first time

title: Putin Declares Victory in Ukraine Inevitable in Victory Day Speech
detail: President Vladimir Putin delivered his Victory Day address on Red Square on May 9, 2026, stating Russia faces 'an aggressive force that is armed and supported by the entire bloc of NATO' and declaring: 'Victory has always been and will be ours.' Putin drew direct parallels between Russia's fight in Ukraine and the Soviet struggle against Nazi Germany in WWII, using the sacred 'Victory Day' symbolism to frame the current war. The speech notably did not announce any major policy changes, territorial claims, or escalation, consistent with the beginning of the Trump-brokered three-day ceasefire. The Kremlin press release was published on the official Kremlin website.

media.caption: Putin speaks at Victory Day parade, declaring Russia fights 'NATO-backed aggression' in Ukraine

title: US-Brokered 3-Day Ceasefire Takes Effect; 1,000-Prisoner Exchange Begins
detail: The US-brokered three-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine officially took effect on May 9, coinciding with Russia's Victory Day. The ceasefire included a halt to all offensive kinetic activity and the exchange of 1,000 prisoners by each side — the largest prisoner swap of 2026. Both President Zelensky and Putin's adviser Yuri Ushakov confirmed implementation. While early reports of ceasefire violations emerged from both sides, the exchange of prisoners proceeded. Trump's statement framed the ceasefire as a potential 'beginning of the end' of the war, though European allies remained cautious that a 72-hour pause would translate into meaningful peace negotiations.

media.caption: Russia and Ukraine begin 3-day ceasefire and prisoner exchange brokered by Trump
